name: John Bennet Lawes
summary: English agricultural scientist and entrepreneur who founded Rothamsted Experimental Station and the artificial fertilizer industry.

name: Dr J H Gilbert
summary: Chemist who collaborated with Lawes for 57 years at Rothamsted on agricultural experiments.

name: Marianne
summary: Mother of John Bennet Lawes who raised him after his father's death.

aliases: His father, also called John Bennet Lawes
name: John Bennet Lawes
summary: Father of John Bennet Lawes who died when the subject was eight.

aliases: that interesting character Sir John Wittewronge
name: Sir John Wittewronge
summary: 17th Century ancestor of Lawes who lived at Rothamsted.

name: Rothamsted Manor
summary: Estate owned by Lawes where the experimental station was founded.

name: Eton
summary: School attended by Lawes.

name: Brasenose College, Oxford
summary: College attended by Lawes where he left without a degree.

name: Rothamsted Experimental Station
summary: Oldest agricultural research station in the world, founded by Lawes in 1843.

name: Deptford factory
summary: Factory set up by Lawes in 1843 to produce superphosphate.

aliases: factory was erected at Barking Creek
name: Barking Creek factory
summary: Larger factory erected later for Lawes' fertilizer business.

name: Lawes Chemical Company
summary: Company that ran Lawes' fertilizer business until sold.

name: Royal Society
summary: Scientific society that elected Lawes as Fellow and awarded him medals.

name: Royal Agricultural Society
summary: Society Lawes was closely connected with from its founding.

name: Chemical Society
summary: Society of which Lawes was a Fellow.

name: Woburn Experimental Station
summary: Experimental station where Lawes started field experiments in 1876.

name: Lawes Agricultural Trust
summary: Trust set up in 1889 to maintain agricultural investigations.

name: Royal Bavarian Academy of Sciences
summary: Academy that awarded Lawes and Gilbert the Liebig Silver Medal.

name: St Nicholas church
summary: Church where Lawes and Gilbert are buried.

name: superphosphate
summary: Fertilizer manufactured by Lawes from mineral phosphates treated with sulphuric acid.

name: Lawes Testimonial Laboratory
summary: Laboratory built with funds collected by farmers and opened in 1855.

name: Mason Laboratory
summary: Small building joining the Testimonial Lab and present laboratory.

name: James Mason Laboratory
summary: Laboratory opened in 1906/7.

name: Russell building
summary: Building completed by 1918 replacing the Testimonial Laboratory.

name: Liebig
summary: German agricultural chemist who controversially disagreed with Lawes on nitrogen.

name: Charles
summary: Son of John Bennet Lawes.

name: Caroline
summary: Daughter of John Bennet Lawes.

name: Edwin Grey
summary: Staff member at Rothamsted from 1872 who wrote reminiscences.

name: Robert Warington
summary: Chemist at Rothamsted from 1876 to 1890 who studied nitrification.

name: Duke of Bedford
summary: Owner of the estate where Woburn experiments were conducted.
